claims.text: A location decision is the choice of the place, or geographical area, in which a business will set up and carry out its operations; a relocation decision is the same choice made again when a business that already operates decides to move.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: The factors most relevant to a manufacturing business location decision typically include closeness to raw materials and component suppliers, the skills and wages of local labour, transport links such as roads, rail and ports, the cost and dependability of the energy supply, room to expand, and government incentives on offer in the area.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: For a service or retail business the factors that usually matter most are closeness to the customers who make up its market, the volume of passing trade a site sees, where competitors stand, how easily customers can reach and park at the site, and the rent for the site.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Selling online shifts, but does not remove, the importance of location for a service business: an online seller still needs premises its staff can reach, and where goods are delivered, depots positioned on the delivery routes matter in much the same way a shopfront once did.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: An international location decision is the choice of which country a business will set up and carry out its operations in; it weighs factors, such as political stability and the country laws, that barely differ between two towns in the same country.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: When deciding which country to locate operations in, a business could consider the cost and skill of labour, the size of the market and the direction it is heading, closeness to materials and to customers, transport links, taxes and government incentives, the country legal system and how strictly its rules are enforced, and political stability.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Low wages in a country do not by themselves mean low unit costs, because output per worker may also be low: the wage saved per hour can be spent again on the extra hours each unit takes to make, so a country with cheaper labour can still produce a dearer unit.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Locating operations in another country often adds costs and risks that stay with the business: the transport needed to reach the market, communication and management across a distance, and the possibility that the country rules or politics change after the investment has been made.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Legal controls on location are rules, set by a government or a local authority, that restrict where a business may build or operate - for example zoning plans that separate industry from housing.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Legal controls shape location decisions by ruling some sites out, by attaching conditions such as limits on noise, delivery hours or the roads lorries may use, and by protecting areas such as residential streets; a business that ignores them may face fines or an order to close.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Legal controls differ between countries, between towns and even between streets, and a local authority can review and redraw its plans, so a business needs to investigate the current rules for a specific site before committing to it.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: To recommend and justify a location is to name the better site for a business in the circumstances given, and to support that choice with reasons drawn from those circumstances, showing why the factors that matter most for this business favour it.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: The most suitable location for a business depends on the type of business and on its objectives: what a low-cost manufacturer needs from a site is often very different from what a service business that lives on passing trade needs.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A well-justified location recommendation weighs the factors that matter most for the business at hand, shows why the alternative site is weaker in those circumstances, and states the conditions the recommendation depends on.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.
